subject: ReadySet evaluation: workload snapshot & trial action items
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira@readyset.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: Nikhil Verma <nverma@readyset.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: trial workload snapshot and questions

Hi Kimberly —

Great to meet earlier. Quick follow-up from our side: we’re excited to run a short evaluation with Redwood to validate latency and cost at scale. High-level notes from the discovery:

- Primary use case: contextual search + short answer generation for customer support.
- Peak user-facing RPS: roughly 140 RPS during business hours; typical sustained baseline of 18–25 RPS outside peaks.
- Token profile: prompt tokens ~ 80–160; average generation tokens ~ 40–60; 99th percentile ~ 350 tokens.
- Concurrency: 40–60 concurrent real-time requests at peak; we also have batched offline jobs that run nightly (not part of this trial).
- Burst patterns: 3–5 minute bursts up to 180 RPS during incident-driven support surges; these occur ~2–3 times/week.

Next asks from our team:
1) Can Redwood outline a trial test plan (smoke + load windows) and suggested acceptance criteria?
2) What data and sample traffic format do you need from us?
3) Typical trial length & Redwood owner for day-to-day coordination.

I attached a CSV with a simple traffic sample and can share a fuller dataset if helpful.

Thanks — Samira
Samira Khan
Head of Platform Engineering, ReadySet
samira@readyset.com
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@readyset.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: trial workload snapshot and questions

Samira — thanks for the clear summary and the sample CSV. Putting a short plan here so we have alignment; Marcus and I will run the technical bits, Aditya is looped for commercial quick-turns.

Summary of what we heard (please confirm):
- Peak RPS ~140, baseline 18–25 RPS, bursts up to 180 RPS for a few minutes, concurrency 40–60.
- Prompt avg 80–160 tokens, gen avg 40–60, p99 ~350 tokens.

Proposed Redwood evaluation plan (high level):
1) Pre-kickoff (3 business days) — exchange sample traffic and creds, set up a private trial endpoint, confirm network egress rules.
2) Smoke test (day 1) — validate correctness, function/tool calls, and streaming for 100 requests.
3) Load window (day 2) — ramp to baseline (25 RPS), then execute two burst tests: short burst 180 RPS for 3 minutes and sustained 140 RPS for 30 minutes. Capture p50/p95/p99 latency, error rates, and GPU utilization.
4) Stability window (days 3–7) — run replayed traffic at baseline for 48 hours and monitor token costs and cache hit rates.
5) Evaluation & wrap (end of week 2) — joint review, go/no-go based on acceptance criteria below.

Suggested acceptance criteria (example):
- Functional: 0 unresolved correctness regressions vs baseline prompt set.
- Latency: p50 < 120 ms, p95 < 400 ms for interactive requests in the baseline profile.
- Reliability: error rate < 0.5% during burst tests.
- Cost: per-1M-token inference cost within 20% of your current overall inference spend target (we’ll refine with your billing team).

Data & format we need: the CSV you attached is perfect for initial runs. Ideally include a column for request_type, prompt_tokens, expected_gen_tokens, and a sample user_id for any session-affinity testing. Send any VPN/IP allowlist or proxy details for the private endpoint.

Owners & contacts:
- Redwood technical lead: Marcus Lin (marcus@redwood.com) — load tests, telemetry
- Redwood sales/ops: Kimberly Park (kimberly@redwood.com) — trial runbook, timelines, PO coordination
- ReadySet technical lead: Samira Khan (samira@readyset.com) — sample data owner

Next steps (actionable):
- Samira: share an expanded sample (CSV or JSONL) and any allowlist info by EOD tomorrow.
- Marcus: will send preliminary load script and recommended sequence names.
- Kimberly: I’ll draft a short trial runbook and attach a PO template for procurement.

I attached the CSV you sent to this thread and a PO draft for quick review.

Best —
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.com

Samira / Kimberly — quick technical clarifications to make the load plan deterministic: 

1) Token distribution: do you see separate cohorts (search vs answer) with different token stats, or is the distribution blended? If separate, can you tag request_type in the sample (search|answer)?
2) Session affinity: are the concurrent requests uniformly distributed across user_ids or concentrated to a smaller set (i.e., hot keys)?
3) Caching: do you expect prefix/KV cache hits from repeated contexts?

Example load profile I’ll prepare once we have answers:
- Baseline: 25 RPS, request mix 70% search / 30% answer, median prompt 100 tokens, gen 50 tokens.
- Burst 1: 180 RPS for 3 minutes (simulate incident surge).
- Burst 2: 140 RPS sustained 30 minutes (peak traffic).
- Concurrency target: 60 concurrent sessions (open connections with streaming).

Telemetry we’ll collect: per-request latency, GPU batch sizes, KV cache hit ratio, per-token CPU/GPU time, and per-route token cost estimate. Please include any internal SLI targets if you have them.

I’ll drop the load harness and a small README into the Drive link once Kimberly confirms.

Thanks —
Marcus Lin
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com
From: Samira Khan <samira@readyset.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-20T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: trial workload snapshot and questions

Thanks — answering Marcus’ items inline: 

1) Distribution: two clear cohorts. Search (70%) — prompt 60–120 tokens / gen 20–40. Answer (30%) — prompt 120–300 / gen 60–250. CSV has a request_type column; I uploaded a larger JSONL to the Drive link.
2) Session affinity: fairly uniform for search, but answers have hot sessions (top 5% of user_ids receive ~25% of requests).
3) Caching: prefix reuse is moderate for search (expected cache hit ~12–15%), low for answer flows.

We can provide an allowlist for Redwood’s trial endpoint (public IPs below) and we’re available to start the trial next Monday (2027-04-26) or Wednesday (2027-04-28).

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C-readyset-eval
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/companies/ReadySet (company record updated with trial objective)

Let us know which start date works; also looping in Nikhil (engineering) who will coordinate procurement signoff.

Samira
